package_info.why_malicious: The report is a high-level overview of the risks posed by open source malware in software supply chains. It does not mention any specific malicious package, version, or code. Instead, it highlights the general threat of attackers weaponizing open source components by inserting malicious code that evades detection and sabotages software projects.

behavioral_signatures: Open source package performing unexpected or hidden actions
Malicious code masquerading as legitimate open source components
Code that evades traditional security detection
file_indicators: Unexpected files or scripts in open source packages
Files with obfuscated or suspicious code in dependencies
network_indicators: Unexpected outbound network connections from open source components
Communication to unknown or suspicious domains initiated by dependencies
detection_knowledge.how_to_detect: Monitor open source dependencies for unexpected behaviors, such as network activity, file system changes, or obfuscated code. Use software composition analysis tools to identify and flag suspicious or recently published packages. Regularly audit dependencies for signs of tampering or malicious code insertion.
